title: W1 DRAFT: ratios for the section-3 invariants and the ledger-anchored P-numbers
description: Wave 1's ratio-determination act, and the reason this is a thinker task rather than a worker's: extracting a clean ratio from prose that mixes rule, precedent and history IS the ratio-identification problem this layer theorizes (docs/precedent-research/02-ratio-identification.md). The drafter DECLARES the ratio; a verifier CONFIRMS it against the source text. Produce, for every wave-1 row of the frozen ledger, the exact publish command and the ratio text, with the source sentence quoted beside it so the text-against-source audit has two texts to put side by side. Wave 1 is the ledger-anchored material: the eight ORCHESTRATION.md section-3 invariants and the standing-force P-numbers. You publish nothing.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY docs/precedent-research/codification-wave1-ratios.md (NEW) plus the ratio text files it references under the same directory. MUST NOT write anything under .harness/, MUST NOT run precedent.py publish against the live registry, MUST NOT edit ORCHESTRATION.md, PRECEDENT.md, INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md, claude.md, gemini.md, state.json or any test file.

INPUT IS THE FROZEN LEDGER, NOT THE SCOUT'S CENSUS: work the wave-1 rows of docs/precedent-research/codification-ledger.md exactly as frozen. Adding a row, dropping a row, or changing a row's tier, subject or wave is a DEVIATION: allowed only with a DEVIATION: note naming the row, the reason, and the new N1 - because the census arithmetic every later task checks against moves with it.

FOR EVERY ROW, THREE ARTIFACTS SIDE BY SIDE: (a) the SOURCE TEXT quoted verbatim from its prose home with path and section; (b) the RATIO exactly as it will be published; (c) the COMPLETE publish command with no ellipsis, passing the ratio via --ratio-file (long text and shell metacharacters: P-021 - your shell expands backticks and dollar-parens before the CLI ever sees them).

THE RATIO STATES THE NORM, NOT THE HISTORY. A ratio that recites what a task fixed instead of what an agent must do is a defect. Read the shape to imitate first: python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py show PR-002 and show PR-004. Every ratio must be readable and actionable by an agent who has never seen the P-number behind it.

WIDER-THAN-SOURCE IS THE FAILURE MODE THIS WAVE CARRIES: a ratio may not bind more broadly than its home text does. Where two homes for one norm diverge in scope - the no-external-LLM rule reads WIDER in ORCHESTRATION.md:180-183 (it extends to local model subprocesses) than in either NLAH - the record names the widest home as primary and states the divergence in dicta rather than silently averaging the two.

CD8 - DOUBLE-HOMED NORMS GET ONE RECORD: every home the ledger lists appears in sources, and the ratio or the validity conditions name which home is primary. The worst case in this wave is producer != approver, which the scout found in six homes; one record, six citations, one named primary.

CD6 - TIER EVIDENCE PER ROW, honestly: the token kinds the CLI enforces are not the same as the tier tradition suggests. An invariant that was bootstrap-seeded at generation 0 has no P-NNN token and therefore cannot honestly publish at tier 2 - it takes the tier its evidence supports, and the record says so. Where the ledger flagged NO-VERIFIABLE-ANCHOR, the drafted record states that plainly.

CD3 - P-023: no drafted ratio may create, backfill or cite-as-resolved P-023, and any record whose subject touches the reopen rule carries a validity condition naming the open gap and T-365 as its owner.

SCOPE_CONDITIONS ARE ROLE-SHAPED, NOT DECORATIVE: follow PR-002's shape (role:X performing Y). They publish UNCONFIRMED and carry persuasive strength only until a distinct identity confirms them (PRECEDENT.md section 6), so no record in this epic may self-confirm and no ratio may lean on its own scope claim for force. VALIDITY CONDITIONS ARE DISTINCT FROM SCOPE: at least one validity entry per record must be mechanically CHECKABLE - a file-line or bare-path form, which is all stale's check V evaluates (.harness/bin/precedent.py _validity_entry_checkable_kind); free text is reported unchecked and never flagged.

TITLE AND SUBJECT DISCIPLINE PER ROW: state the title's character count (hard cap 80, refusal at exit 1) and confirm the subject slug is unique against the live registry (python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py list --json).

SELF-CHECK - DRY-RUN EVERY COMMAND IN A UNIQUELY-NAMED THROWAWAY ROOT, never against the live registry: python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py publish --root <scratch>/w1-dryrun-<something-only-you-would-pick> ... . The scratchpad namespace is shared across identities and a generic name silently contaminated a prior measurement (the measured T-375 lesson), so the name must be unique to you. Paste each id and exit code, and confirm the throwaway root's final record count equals N1 exactly.

TEST FLOOR (P-025): python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py" prints a 'Ran N tests' line with N >= 252 and OK (252 measured live 2026-08-13 by the planner; if N is higher, name T-376 as the landed repair rather than absorbing the delta). Also git status --porcelain .harness/bin/ empty, proving you modified no code.

HAND OFF to verifier (never self-mark done) with the per-row table (ledger row, subject, tier, tier_evidence tokens, title char count, dry-run id) and every OPEN-QUESTION: the drafting exposed - especially any row whose home text turned out not to support the tier the ledger assigned. LEAK AND STYLE HYGIENE (the board and .harness/tasks/*.json are tracked): no absolute filesystem path, no username and no emoji in any note or artifact you write. Temp-root replays print absolute paths - redact them to a placeholder before pasting. Two prior tasks leaked an operator home path exactly this way.
